title: Multiple backgrounds and background clipping
learningObjectives: Explain multiple backgrounds and background clipping and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: An element can have multiple background layers separated by commas. The first listed image is painted closest to the user. background-position, background-size, background-repeat, and background-origin/background-clip can be specified per layer. background-clip controls the area in which the background is painted.
understand.whyItMatters: Multiple layers allow gradients and images to combine without extra markup. Carefully align each layer's position and size, and ensure text remains readable over the resulting background.
understand.analogy: Multiple backgrounds are like transparent sheets stacked on a surface; the first layer sits visually above later layers.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The linear gradient overlays the radial gradient. The background is clipped to the padding box.

examples.explanation: The linear gradient overlays the radial gradient. The background is clipped to the padding box.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered visual example demonstrating the CSS effect.

practise.guidedTask: Create a panel with two background layers and different positions. Add a border and compare background-clip values.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

questions.prompt: Which background layer is painted closest to the user?
questions.explanation: The first background image layer is painted on top of subsequent background layers.

questions.prompt: What should accompany a decorative CSS effect?
options: Readable content and a usable fallback

questions.answer: Readable content and a usable fallback
questions.explanation: Decorative effects should enhance content rather than become the only way to access it.
